title: Precision Clock Generation with Reference Clock Loss Tolerant Dynamic Tuning to Enable Crystal Less SSD
problem: SSD controllers rely on crystal oscillators (XTAL) for accurate reference clocks to PLLs. XTALs incur BOM cost and increase PCB complexity. Host may disable its clock before SSD completes data transfer to NAND, requiring fallback precision clock generation.
motivation: Removing XTAL reduces cost and PCB design complexity. A hybrid clock selection mechanism can maintain PLL accuracy during data transfer and tolerate reference clock loss during backend operations.
method: Clock multiplexer selecting between host-provided clock and internal relaxation oscillator. Control logic ensures continuous clock availability without external indication or frequency glitch. PLL operates at highest accuracy with incoming data, lower accuracy for backend completion.
key_novelty: Autonomous crystal-free SSD clock generation via dynamic host/internal clock selection with seamless switching, no external control signals, and graceful accuracy degradation.
contributions: Novel reference clock loss tolerant PLL input multiplexer
Seamless clock selection without frequency glitch
Lab validation on actual SSD use cases

metrics.clock_accuracy: high during data transfer, lower during backend

limitations: Abstract only; no quantitative accuracy or frequency stability metrics provided; no comparison with other crystal-free approaches.
primary_theme: Specialized analog circuit design for cost reduction
